hypotheses.statement: The average total amount per yellow taxi trip on Monday 2025-01-20 was higher than the average of the other three Mondays in January 2025 (2025-01-06, 2025-01-13, 2025-01-27).
hypotheses.support_if: avg_total_amount on 2025-01-20 > mean(avg_total_amount on 2025-01-06, 2025-01-13, 2025-01-27) by a meaningful margin (e.g., >5%).
hypotheses.refute_if: avg_total_amount on 2025-01-20 is within 5% of the baseline Mondays' average.

hypotheses.statement: Monday 2025-01-20 was Martin Luther King Jr. Day (a federal holiday), which changed the passenger mix (e.g., more tourists, fewer commuters) and/or trip characteristics (longer trips, higher fares) compared to regular Mondays.
hypotheses.support_if: us_holidays shows a federal holiday on 2025-01-20 (MLK Day) and not on the other Mondays; trip count on 2025-01-20 differs significantly from baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.refute_if: 2025-01-20 is not a holiday, or trip count and avg_total_amount patterns match baseline Mondays.

hypotheses.statement: Adverse weather on 2025-01-20 (e.g., snow, rain, extreme cold) caused longer trips, more surcharges, or a shift to taxi from other modes, raising avg_total_amount.
hypotheses.support_if: nyc_weather_daily shows precipitation, snowfall, or extreme temperatures on 2025-01-20 that are absent on baseline Mondays; avg_trip_distance also higher on 2025-01-20.
hypotheses.refute_if: Weather on 2025-01-20 is similar to baseline Mondays (no precipitation, similar temps).

hypotheses.statement: The fare composition on 2025-01-20 shifted toward higher-fare components (e.g., more tolls, tips, surcharges, or longer distances) compared to baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.support_if: avg_trip_distance on 2025-01-20 is higher than baseline; if trip-level data were available, tolls/tips/surcharges would be higher. With daily aggregates, we check avg_trip_distance and trip count as proxies.
hypotheses.refute_if: avg_trip_distance and trip count on 2025-01-20 are in line with baseline Mondays.

hypotheses.statement: The geographic mix of trips on 2025-01-20 shifted toward zones with higher average fares (e.g., more airport trips, Manhattan core) compared to baseline Mondays.
hypotheses.support_if: If zone-level data were available, we would see a higher share of trips from high-fare zones on 2025-01-20. With current tables, we can only infer from distance and count proxies.
hypotheses.refute_if: No proxy evidence of zone mix shift (distance, count stable).

hypotheses.statement: The spike on 2025-01-20 is an artifact of data quality issues (e.g., missing trips, duplicate records, fare calculation errors) rather than a real change.
hypotheses.support_if: Trip count on 2025-01-20 is anomalously low or high vs baseline; avg_total_amount is an extreme outlier (>3 std dev from baseline mean).
hypotheses.refute_if: Trip count and avg_total_amount on 2025-01-20 are within normal variation of baseline Mondays.

queries.purpose: Get avg_total_amount, trips, avg_trip_distance for target Monday 2025-01-20 and baseline Mondays 2025-01-06, 2025-01-13, 2025-01-27. Compute target vs baseline average.
Check if 2025-01-20 is a federal holiday (MLK Day) and confirm other Mondays are not holidays. Join yellow_daily with us_holidays on trip_date=holiday_date for the four Mondays.
Get weather (prcp_mm, snow_mm, tmax_c, tmin_c) for 2025-01-20 and the three baseline Mondays. Compare for anomalies.
Compare avg_trip_distance and trips on 2025-01-20 vs baseline Mondays as proxies for fare mix changes (longer trips, different volume).
Assess data quality: check if trips on 2025-01-20 is an outlier (e.g., <50% or >150% of baseline mean) and if avg_total_amount is >3 std dev from baseline mean.

plan.rationale: H0 quantifies the metric jump. H1 tests the holiday hypothesis (MLK Day). H2 tests weather impact. H3 uses available daily aggregates (distance, count) as proxies for fare mix. H4 (zone_mix) cannot be directly tested with current tables (no zone-level daily data), so we note it and rely on proxies. H5 checks for data quality issues. All queries use only catalog tables and stay within the 2024-04-01..2025-02-28 window.
